domains.original: First-countable topological time, measurable sample space, topological measurable state with measurable open sets.
domains.reconstructed: The same spaces T, Ω and E, with every state open set measurable.
domains.evidence: The time and state typeclass requirements and the sample measurable structure match the source. A full Borel equality or compact state is unnecessary.

quantifiers.original: Each time slice is measurable. A single full-measure sample event has continuous whole paths.
quantifiers.reconstructed: All slices are measurable, and μ-almost every ω has a continuous whole path on T.
quantifiers.evidence: `∀ t, Measurable (X t)` and `∀ᵐ ω, Continuous (fun t => X t ω)` have the stated order.

assumptions.original: Probability measure, measurable slices and a.e. whole-path continuity.
assumptions.reconstructed: Same, with the same first countability and measurable-open hypotheses.
assumptions.evidence: The target theorem has no joint measurability, filtration, integrability or finite-dimensional state assumption.

conclusion.original: The actual marginal-law map is continuous for the weak topology of bounded continuous tests.
conclusion.reconstructed: The same marginal-law map is continuous into weak probability measures.
conclusion.evidence: Lean `Continuous (fun t => μ.map (hX t).aemeasurable)` uses the weak topology on `ProbabilityMeasure`. The displayed test-function characterization is equivalent.

scopes.original: Continuity at every time in T, obtained from the same whole-path a.e. hypothesis.
scopes.reconstructed: Continuity on T in the weak topology.
scopes.evidence: The proof fixes t only after the whole-path premise. Its pointwise use does not replace the premise by separate time-dependent events.

constant_dependencies.original: No scalar constants, rates, horizon parameters or auxiliary law curves.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The measures and neighborhoods depend only on X, P and the specified time. First countability supplies a filter property, not a numerical choice.
